zh.title: 洛克希德馬汀簽署MOU 尋求本土戰機鈧金屬供應
zh.summary: 洛克希德馬汀與礦業開發商 NioCorp 簽署不具約束力的備忘錄，探討在未來十年每年購買最多15公噸氧化鈧，用於戰機結構與積層製造，降低對中國供應的依賴。
body: 洛克希德馬汀（Lockheed Martin）於2026年8月5日發布消息，該公司已與礦物開發商 NioCorp Developments 簽署一份不具約束力的諒解備忘錄（MOU），探討在未來十年內每年向 NioCorp 購買最多15公噸的氧化鈧，或以鋁鈧合金形式交貨。
這項安排延伸自雙方自2025年10月啟動的聯合開發計畫，該計畫獲美國國防部依據《國防生產法》撥款1000萬美元，由洛克希德馬汀旗下臭鼬工廠（Skunk Works）與 NioCorp 共同為戰機生產鋁鈧合金原型零件。
NioCorp 董事長兼執行長 Mark Smith 指出，這份備忘錄顯示減少美國在鈧金屬上對中國依賴的論據更加充分。鈧以極低比例添加至鋁合金中即可提升強度、耐腐蝕性與可焊接性，適合用於機身結構及積層製造。
不過，AeroTime 報導指出，NioCorp 位於 Elk Creek 的礦場計畫雖已在2026年2月展開坑道開挖，但整體專案尚未完全取得融資與投產。該公司正向美國進出口銀行尋求最高8億美元的債務融資，申請自2023年提交後仍待最終批准。
報導也提及，全球鈧市場規模極小。美國地質調查局（USGS）估計2025年全球氧化鈾消費量僅60公噸，且中國是最大生產國。美國在2025年並無商業開採或回收任何鈾，完全仰賴進口。

en.title: Lockheed Martin signs MOU for domestic fighter scandium supply amid China export controls
en.summary: Lockheed Martin has signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding with minerals developer NioCorp covering the potential purchase of up to 15 tonnes of scandium oxide per year over the next decade, aiming to reduce U.S. dependence on Chinese supply for fighter aircraft manufacturing.
body: Lockheed Martin has signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding with minerals developer NioCorp Developments covering the potential purchase of up to 15 tonnes of scandium oxide a year over the next decade, NioCorp announced on August 4, 2026. The material could be delivered either as oxide or as aluminum-scandium alloy.

Tyler Robinson, vice president for technology roadmaps at Lockheed Martin Skunk Works, said the company appreciated NioCorp’s work on domestic sourcing and alloying and would continue to evaluate that supply as part of its wider alloy development effort. NioCorp chairman and chief executive Mark Smith framed the agreement as evidence that the argument for reducing U.S. dependence on China for scandium had strengthened.

The MOU extends a joint development program announced in October 2025, under which NioCorp and Skunk Works are producing prototype aluminum-scandium alloy components for fighter aircraft. That work draws on a $10 million award from the U.S. Department of Defense under Title III of the Defense Production Act.

However, the wider Elk Creek project is not yet fully financed or in production. NioCorp began constructing the mine portal in February 2026 but is still seeking up to $800 million in debt financing from the U.S. Export-Import Bank, with the application remaining subject to due diligence and final approval since its submission in 2023.

Scandium added to aluminum in fractions of a percent improves strength, corrosion resistance and weldability with little weight penalty, making it attractive for airframe structures and additive manufacturing. But the market remains extremely small: the U.S. Geological Survey put global consumption of scandium oxide at just 60 tonnes in 2025, with China the leading producer and the United States wholly import-dependent.
